# Interview

Build the ontology from the user's own words. Ask plain questions, record exactly what the user said, and let the
kit rank what to ask next. `O` is `python3 plugins/general-ontology/bin/onto`, run from the topic repo root; prefer the `onto_*` MCP tools when this harness has them. Follow
the reading rules of the **onto** skill.

## 1. No ontology yet

Run `O doctor`. Its `where` line says whether this folder is a template checkout, a topic or neither.

**Neither.** A template checkout is a clone of the template whose repo root holds
`plugins/general-ontology/ontokit/`. Anywhere else, do not run `init` or `setup`. A topic started there has no
vendored kit (so kit upgrades never reach it) and no CI, and may lack the git rules that keep the raw, unredacted
`inbox/` out of commits. Tell the user to clone the template first (README, Quick start), then open the clone and
start again.

**A template checkout.** Run the setup interview: one question per turn, as in section 3, skipping any the user
already answered. `plugins/general-ontology/docs/setup-interview.md` (linked from `AGENTS.md`, section 1) has each
question with why it matters, an example answer, its options and what it records.

**In a cloud agent** (a machine discarded after the session, such as cloud Devin), read
`plugins/general-ontology/docs/cloud-agents.md` first. Never run `--new` there without a remote: the folder is
lost with the machine. Recommend that the user runs `./new-topic` on their own machine, pushes the topic to a
private remote and adds that repo to the agent; or ask question 4 for a remote only, pass `--origin <url>`, and
push right after setup with the user's yes.

In short:

1. What the ontology is about: the title, and the user's sentence as the summary. Suggest a title ("Community
   garden"), a topic slug (for example `community-garden`) and a namespace (lower case, `garden`) from it, and
   confirm all three in one line, saying that no command changes the title later: `--name` and `--ns`; the title
   and the sentence go in the file's `setup` object (`title`, `summary`).
2. What it should help them do or decide: an `answers` item for `q.frame.goal`, with a `name` the user confirmed
   when its first sentence is not a short name of the goal (an example such as "Like when I ...").
3. Where it should live: `--new ~/Ontologies/<slug>` (recommended), `--here` (this kit checkout becomes the
   topic, so new topics need another checkout: confirm it once more first, as AGENTS.md says), or a folder they
   type, which goes in the file as `setup.new` (a full path) and then the setup line has no `--new`. When the
   folder is cloud-synced, warn and add `--cloud-ok` only if they keep it. Skipped, it is `~/Ontologies/<slug>`.
4. Who else works on it and where it is backed up: `--origin <url>` for a private git remote. For "just me" or
   "decide later", add the decision to the answers file instead.
5. How sensitive the input is: `--personal keep`, `redact` (recommended) or `refuse`. Only as the flag, never in
   the `decisions` list. Say what each does: `redact` takes out emails, phone numbers, ids and card numbers,
   `refuse` refuses text holding them, and no setting finds people's names in prose. Map a free-text reply to the
   closest option and confirm it with the user.
6. Whether to track risks and controls: yes adds `--packs assessment`.
7. Which agents will open this topic? More than one may be picked: Claude Code, Devin, Codex, Cursor, Copilot,
   Gemini or another agent, passed as `--agent claude,devin` (`claude`, `devin`, `codex`, `cursor`, `copilot`,
   `gemini`, `generic`). Without it, setup wires Claude Code alone.
7a. Only when Claude Code is one of them: install the plugin for this repo (`--plugin project`, recommended) or run
   without installing (`--plugin plugin-dir`).

Write what they said, in their words, to the gitignored `.onto/` folder as `.onto/setup.json`, and update it every
turn (there is no topic yet, so no `onto_answer` and no checkpoint; show `setup 3/7` as the progress line). The
answers that map to flags go in its `setup` object (`title`, `summary`, `name`, `ns`, `new` as a full path, `here`,
`origin`, `personal`, `packs`, `agent`, `plugin`), and the numbers of skipped questions in `skipped`, so on "stop"
the file holds everything: the next session asks only what it lacks. The user's own words stay in the file, never on the
command line, where the shell would read them. A decisions item for a choice that has a flag (location,
sensitivity, a remote URL, a pack, the agents, the plugin) is refused: pass the flag.
A run with no failed step moves the file to `.onto/setup.<slug>.done.json` (personal data redacted as the topic's
policy says; delete it once the topic is set up), so a `.onto/setup.json` you find is always a stopped interview. Decisions use the question words setup records them under; a flag passed in the same
run wins over a file item for the same question:

```json
{"setup": {"title": "Community garden",
           "summary": "Running our community garden: plots, crops and the people who tend them."},
 "answers": [{"q": "q.frame.goal", "text": "Decide which beds to rotate each season"}],
 "decisions": [{"question": "Will anyone else work on it, and where is it backed up?",
                "options": ["solo=just me, no remote for now", "remote=a private git remote", "later=decide later"],
                "chosen": "solo"}]}
```

Then run setup in the repo root with the flags the answers map to:

```
O setup --new ~/Ontologies/<slug> --name <slug> --ns <ns> --personal redact --agent claude --plugin project --answers @.onto/setup.json --launch none
```

Leave `--new ~/Ontologies/<slug>` out when the file holds `setup.new` or `setup.here`: a `--new` that names
another folder wins over the user's answer (setup then says so and records no location decision). Setup checks
every value of the file first (question ids, choices against their options, credentials, personal data the
`--personal` choice refuses), so a bad value fails the run before anything is written.

Setup does README step 1 (`git checkout -b main && git remote rename origin kit`), runs `O init`, adds the packs,
replays the answers, records the user's choices as decisions (only because they came with `--answers`), commits
("Start <slug>") once `inbox/` and `.onto/` are ignored, wires the plugin (Claude Code) and writes the other
agents' files (the `agents` step). Every step says `done`, `already` or `skipped (reason)`; it is safe to run
again. Do not run `O init` yourself in a template checkout: it refuses until step 1 is done, and setup does it.

Show the checklist. When a step says `failed` (exit 1), give the user its detail, which names the fix (on a new
machine, often git's `user.name` and `user.email`), and run the same command again once it is fixed; do not hand
over `Next:` lines then, except when only the `plugin` step failed (offline, or no git credentials claude can use
for a private template): the topic is ready; hand its `Next:` lines over with the plugin step's detail. With `--here`, the session is already in the topic: go on to section 2. With `--new`, give the
user setup's `Next:` lines (the folder, and one line per chosen agent: "open it in Claude Code and say: start the
ontology"; for another agent, "open the folder and ask the agent to follow AGENTS.md"), and the paste blocks after
them, for the parts set in an agent's own app. The new session finds the setup questions recorded and
starts the quick start.

If the user wants the Claude Code plugin installed by hand, the README (Manual setup, step 2) says how.

## 2. Say where things stand

Call `onto_status` and say it in one line: the stage, richness and what is pending ("Stage 2 of 9, data. Richness 34
(sketch). 2 proposals wait for review."). Pending proposals first? Offer **onto-review**, then continue.

Then follow the state (the table in `AGENTS.md`, section 1):

- **Returning** (the status names a checkpoint, or shows a stage past 0 without one): say "welcome back", give the
  checkpoint's next steps and open questions (`O log --last`), or without a checkpoint sum up what `O log` shows
  was recorded last, and the progress line. Offer once any setup choice recorded as "later"
  (`onto_decisions scope=["setup"]`), then continue from there.
- **Fresh topic**: before the quick start, ask the setup questions 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 that are still open; 1 and 3 are
  settled by being here. Ask 7a only when Claude Code is one of the agents and its skills are not loaded yet.
  `onto_decisions scope=["setup"]` lists the recorded choices; the goal (2) is an answer, open while `onto_next`
  still lists `q.frame.goal`. Write the answers to `.onto/setup.json`, then run
  `O setup --answers @.onto/setup.json --launch none` in the topic with the flags they map to (`--origin`,
  `--personal`, `--packs assessment`, `--agent`, `--plugin` only when asked: without it setup keeps the recorded
  plugin choice or the mode an earlier run here tried, or leaves the wiring alone). It replays the goal
  (also after an earlier skip), adds the pack and the remote and records the decisions. When the title is still the
  placeholder ("My topic"), tell the user no command changes it; a fresh topic can be made again with `--title`.
  Never record sensitivity (5) with `onto_decide` or in the file: setup records it only when the policy already
  matches, and when it prints "--personal ... not applied", follow `AGENTS.md`, section 1, "Setup questions in a
  fresh topic".
- **Deepen** (stage 9): offer to ingest new material (**onto-ingest**), review proposals (**onto-review**) or
  deliver something (**onto-deliver**); keep asking gap questions when the user wants.

## 3. The loop

1. Call `onto_next n=1` (`O next`). Each question has an id, the words to ask, why it matters, its `options` and
   `follow_ups`, its `fills` (the kinds it records and the `fields` it sets; `O next` prints the fields as
   `sets:`), and, for gap questions, the node it is about. Set every listed field (in `attrs`) from the same
   answer, so the kit does not ask for it again: for `q.frame.deliverable`, the `audience` as well as the `serves`
   link. The result's `progress` holds the stage, the quick
   start count and the answered and skipped counts; `O next` prints them as the progress line
   (`stage 0 frame | quick start 0/5 | answered 0, skipped 0`).
2. Ask **one question per turn**, in your own words, keeping `{name}` and `{topic}` filled in. Ask up to 3 only for
   short factual questions the user asked to batch. Give one line on why it matters (the item's `why`) and an
   example answer you write yourself, in the topic's words (the kit gives none). When the question has `options`,
   list them as numbered plain-text options. Always offer "skip", "later", "n/a" (not applicable) and "why?". Show the progress line
   every turn.
3. Probe once when an answer is vague or a list is cut short ("Anyone else?", "Can you give one example?"). The
   probe turn records nothing; the next turn records the first answer and the reply together, the more specific
   one first (a goal is named after the first sentence).
4. Draft ops from each answer (the op format is in `../onto-ingest/references/extraction.md`):
   - A fact the user stated gets `basis: "stated"` and a provenance entry `{"quote": "<their exact words>",
     "by": "user"}`. Leave `src` and `loc` out: `onto_answer` stores the answer as an interview source and fills in
     both. The `loc` it writes is `Q:` plus the question id before any `@`, so an answer to the gap question
     `q.gap.orphan@term:rota` is cited as `Q:q.gap.orphan`. A `loc` you write yourself never keeps the `@` part.
   - The quote must be a verbatim part of the answer text. Anything you infer gets `basis: "inferred"`; it lands
     as a draft for review. An inferred change to a confirmed record holds its whole answer for review, so give it
     an answer of its own. An `invoke` line goes in confirmed only when a quote holds it word for word.
   - Reuse existing ids: `onto_search` a name before you add a node for it.
   - A statement the plan depends on ("the water tap stays on all season") is a `premise`; link what depends on
     it with `rests_on`.
   - Link every new node in the same answer. A node without a link does not count toward coverage and comes back
     as an orphan question. An inferred link lands as a draft and comes back as `q.gap.draft_link.<key>@<id>`
     (asked again when another link is drafted): an `add_edge` op of the same link with `basis: "stated"` and the user's yes as the quote confirms it. A term gets a `defines` edge from `topic:<ns>`, or from the process or deliverable that
     uses the word (example in `references/recap-examples.md`).
5. Record the answer in the same turn: `onto_answer q=<id> text="<the answer>" ops=[...] apply=true`. On the CLI,
   write the user's words and the ops under the gitignored `.onto/` folder, never on the shell line (it reads `$`,
   backticks and quotes): `O answer <q> --text-file .onto/answer.txt --ops @.onto/ops.json --apply`.
   Stated, quoted facts are accepted at once; the rest become drafts. A merge, an archive, a change to a
   confirmed record and a pack change (a new kind, relation or question: `add_kind` and the like) need
   `confirm=true` (`--confirm`): show the preview and ask first, the one time an answer gets its own OK turn. If the preview comes back `refused` (problem lines by op number), fix every problem and call
   again; never ask the user to approve a refused preview. `init` creates `topic:<ns>` as confirmed, so filling in
   its summary (the gap question `q.gap.thin@topic:<ns>`) needs `confirm=true` too.
6. Fold the recap into the next turn: start it with "Noted: ..." in at most 3 lines, then ask the next question.
   Wording is in `references/recap-examples.md`.
7. Pick the next question. The `onto_answer` result names the best one. When the answer named something new, ask
   its follow-up next: `onto_next about=<id>` (`O next --about <id>`) puts that node's gap questions and the
   follow-ups first. Never re-ask an answered question; `onto_next` leaves them out, and `O log` shows what was
   recorded when you are unsure.
   **After the quick start, the main kinds.** Once the five quick questions are handled, the kit names
   `q.vocab.kinds` next (flagged `after_quick`), before stage 1 and before any gap question: "What are the main
   kinds of things in {topic}? Name a few, with one example of each." The kinds become the topic's own
   vocabulary. Example answer for a garden: "Beds, crops and harvests. The north bed is a bed, tomatoes are a crop,
   and the July harvest is a harvest." Propose each kind as a local kind (`add_kind`) plus one linked node per
   example (`references/recap-examples.md` has the ops); reuse a kind the topic already has rather than add a
   twin. The `add_kind` ops need `confirm=true`: show the preview, ask, then record it confirmed. Then continue
   with `onto_next`.
8. Skips: `onto_answer q=<id> status=skipped` (or `later`, `na`, `skip_stage` for "skip this whole stage"). `na`
   on a stage question closes its dimension, so nothing more is asked about it; `na` on a gap question
   (`q.gap.*@<id>`) closes only that question. `next` leaves out a question skipped or put off
   (`later`) in the last 2 days and names it under `held_back`. An item flagged `put_off` is listed only when nothing
   else is open; ask it only if the user wants to come back to it. "Why?" gets the question's `why` line, then the
   same question again.

## 4. Choices are decisions

When an answer picks between options ("per bed, not per steward"), also call `onto_decide` in the user's words:
the question, the options as `id=label`, `chosen` (or `other` with `chosen_text`), the rationale and the scope ids.
A change of mind is a new decision with `supersedes`; a detail inside an earlier decision is a new decision
with `narrows` (the earlier one stays active). An answer to a conflict question
(`q.gap.conflict.<field>@<id>`) records its own decision, scoped `<id>#attrs.<field>`, and says so in its notes: do
not record a second one. A conflict settles only through a decision with that scope; set the question n/a to leave
it open on purpose.

## 5. Report progress

Every 5 answers, report the richness change from the version line or `onto_gaps section=summary`
("richness 34 -> 41: people and data are now covered; vocabulary is still empty"). Richness is a heuristic; the
parts are the facts.

## 6. Material instead of answers

If the user pastes notes, drops a file or gives a URL, hand off to **onto-ingest**, then come back to the loop.

## 7. When the user stops

The user can say "stop" at any time. Write a checkpoint so the next session can resume. The open questions are
often the user's own words, so write each list to a file under `.onto/` (one item per line, with a file tool or a
quoted heredoc) and pass the files, never the words on the shell line:

```
O log --checkpoint --done-file .onto/done.txt --next-file .onto/next.txt --open-questions-file .onto/open.txt
```

For example `.onto/done.txt` holds "quick start" and "people" on two lines, `.onto/next.txt` "data owners" and
`.onto/open.txt` "who keeps the harvest log". The next session reads it from `onto_status`.

A "stop" on the OK turn of a preview (step 5 of the loop): the preview stored nothing, not even the answer. Before
the checkpoint, record the answer in the user's words with only the ops that need no `confirm=true` and do not use
the held change (`onto_answer q=<id> text="<the answer>" ops=[...] apply=true`, or with no ops when none are left),
and name the held change in the checkpoint's open questions (a line "confirm the new kind hive" in
`.onto/open.txt`, passed as `--open-questions-file .onto/open.txt`), so the next session offers it again.

Then offer to commit the session, so git holds an undo point for the next one:

```
git check-ignore -q inbox/ && git check-ignore -q .onto/ && echo "inbox and .onto are ignored"
O scan .
git status --short
git add -A && git commit -m "Interview: quick start and people"
```

Only topic files belong in the commit. `inbox/` holds the raw, unredacted input and `.onto/` the kit's state, and a
template clone gitignores both. If the first line prints nothing, never run `git add -A`: tell the user that the raw
inbox would be committed, and let them add `inbox/` and `.onto/` to their `.gitignore` first. When the status list
shows anything other than topic files, name it to the user and let them decide before committing. Commit when the
user says yes, and never push unless they ask. In a cloud agent, the machine and every unpushed commit go when
the session ends: offer to push a session branch and open a pull request, as
`plugins/general-ontology/docs/cloud-agents.md` says. A yes to that offer is the user asking.

Stage goals, the quick start and when a stage counts as done: `references/stages.md`.
